title: 'A distinct Canadian character': The 1920s paintings that changed how the world saw Canada
facts: The Group of Seven was Canada's first internationally recognized national art movement.
FH Varley painted 'Stormy Weather, Georgian Bay' in 1921.
Katerina Atanassova serves as senior curator of Canadian art at The National Gallery of Canada.
Canada celebrates Group of Seven Day on July 7.
The Group of Seven included artists Franklin Carmichael, Lawren Harris, AY Jackson, Franz Johnston, Arthur Lismer, JEH MacDonald, and FH Varley.
Artist Tom Thomson died in 1917 before the official formation of the Group of Seven.
Tom Thomson painted the celebrated Canadian works 'The Jack Pine' and 'The West Wind'.
Lawren Harris painted the artwork 'North Shore, Lake Superior'.
JEH MacDonald and Lawren Harris visited an exhibition of Scandinavian art in Buffalo in 1913.
The Group of Seven art collective officially formed in 1920.
Paintings by the Group of Seven were exhibited at the British Empire Exhibition at Wembley in 1924.
The Professional Native Indian Artists Incorporated (PNIAI) was founded in the early 1970s.
The seven founding members of the PNIAI were Jackson Beardy, Eddy Cobiness, Alex Janvier, Norval Morrisseau, Daphne Odjig, Carl Ray, and Joseph Sanchez.
Michelle LaVallee is Director of the Indigenous Ways and Decolonization Department at the National Gallery of Canada.
Paintings by the Group of Seven are displayed at the National Gallery of Canada in Ottawa.
